reasoning:
All factual claims in the finding are verified against source.

(1) CLAUDE.md line 53 states: 'Custom @intrinsic functions are used for >16-byte structs (decimal 24B, varint 24B) and interval (16B but needs repacking).' This is false in two ways: (a) ducklib.py defines zero @intrinsic functions (grep -n '@intrinsic' ducklib.py returns no output); (b) there are no per-type custom intrinsics for decimal, varint, or interval anywhere in the numbduck tree.

(2) The actual implementations are plain @cres wrappers calling the generic numbox _call_lib_func: duckdb_bind_interval at ducklib.py:1422-1425 and duckdb_bind_decimal at ducklib.py:1428-1431 are both standard _call_lib_func calls with no special ABI handling in ducklib itself.

(3) The real @intrinsic that handles the ABI complexity for these types is numbox's _call_lib_func (numbox/core/bindings/call.py:21), which is a generic @intrinsic that classifies structs and applies eightbyte repacking for interval {i32,i32,i64} internally. numbox's docstring at call.py:21-40 confirms it handles >16-byte structs via pointer+byval+optnone on SysV and handles the {i32,i32,i64} interval repack — exactly the mechanism CLAUDE.md attributes to nonexistent per-type ducklib intrinsics.

(4) No alternative location for these custom intrinsics was found. grep for @intrinsic across the entire numbduck tree returns only the CLAUDE.md line itself (as quoted text) plus review/doc files — zero code definitions.

Severity medium is appropriate: this is a documentation defect in the primary developer guide (CLAUDE.md) with no runtime impact, but it creates a false mental model that per-type custom intrinsics exist in ducklib for decimal/varint/interval, which would misdirect any contributor debugging struct ABI issues or attempting to add similar types.
